findings.evidence: `lang="translanguage"`
findings.fix: Set `lang` to the actual content language, e.g. `lang="en"`.
findings.violation: "translanguage" is not a valid BCP 47 language code, so the declared document language is meaningless to browsers and assistive technology (affects voice selection, translation prompts, etc.).

findings.evidence: `<title id="head-title"></title>`
findings.fix: Add a descriptive title, e.g. "Rider Service Updates".
findings.violation: The page title is empty, so browser tabs, bookmarks, history, and screen readers have no name for the page.

findings.evidence: `Plan a trip\nAccessibility`
findings.fix: Add a skip link (e.g. `Skip to main content`) as the first focusable element.
findings.violation: There is no "skip to main content" link before the nav, forcing keyboard and screen-reader users to tab through navigation on every page load before reaching the content.

findings.evidence: `<div id="main-content">`
findings.fix: Change the wrapper to `<main id="main-content">`.
findings.violation: The primary content region is a generic `div` rather than a `<main>` landmark, so assistive technology users can't jump directly to it.

findings.evidence: both paragraphs end with "Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Write a distinct, accurate closing sentence for each paragraph (or remove it if station staff can't actually help with real-time arrival checks).
findings.violation: The identical trailing sentence is reused for two unrelated actions (fare adjustments vs. checking real-time arrivals), which reads as copy-pasted boilerplate rather than accurate per-topic guidance.

findings.evidence: ``
findings.fix: Add a descriptive `alt` attribute (or `alt=""` if purely decorative).
findings.violation: The image has no `alt` attribute at all, so screen readers will announce the filename or nothing meaningful.

findings.evidence: `<h2 id="s1-h">` ... followed later by `<h4 id="s2-h">`
findings.fix: Change `s2-h` to an `<h2>` (or add an intervening `<h3>` section) to keep heading levels sequential.
findings.violation: The heading level jumps from h2 to h4, skipping h3, which breaks the document outline for screen-reader users navigating by heading level.

findings.evidence: heading "Accessibility improvements" followed by content about reporting service issues and an on-time status table
findings.fix: Rename the heading to match the actual content (e.g. "Service status") or replace the content with genuine accessibility information.
findings.violation: The section heading promises accessibility-related content, but the body text and table are about issue reporting and zone status, unrelated to accessibility.

findings.evidence: "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." (also appears verbatim in `s3-p2`)
findings.fix: Tailor each paragraph's closing sentence to the specific action it follows.
findings.violation: The same sentence is attached both to "report a service issue" and to "review the updated schedule," two different actions, making it unclear which process the one-business-day update timeline actually applies to.

findings.evidence: `<table id="s2-table1">` with no `<caption>`
findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Current zone status".
findings.violation: The table has no caption or accessible name, so screen-reader users get no context for what "Zone/Status" refers to when landing on the table.

findings.evidence: "Passengers can report a service issue at any station kiosk." vs. `s2-p1`'s "Passengers can report a service issue by calling rider services."
findings.fix: Combine into a single statement listing both channels, or explicitly note "You can also report issues by calling rider services" for consistency.
findings.violation: The same action (reporting a service issue) is described in two separate sections via two different channels with no cross-reference, implying they may be different procedures rather than two options for the same one.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: State the actual date or link directly to where it's posted.
findings.violation: "the posted effective date" is vague and self-referential - it doesn't say where that date is posted or link to it, giving the reader no way to find the actual date.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Replace with wording accurate to a lookup action (no confirmation message), and reconcile with `s1-p2` so the two mentions of checking arrivals are consistent.
findings.violation: Checking real-time arrivals is a read-only lookup, not a submitted request, so "a confirmation message follows once the request is processed" (copied from `s3-p1`'s issue-reporting flow) doesn't logically apply here; this also duplicates `s1-p2`'s "check real time arrivals" topic via yet another channel.

findings.evidence: `<button type="button" class="btn-secondary" id="s3-button1">Refresh status</button>`
findings.fix: Associate the button with the status element it updates (e.g. `aria-controls="s3-statuscard"`) and define/implement its action.
findings.violation: The button has no associated behavior or indication of what it refreshes (no linked status region via `aria-controls`, no visible effect described).

findings.evidence: `aria-label="Delete item"` with no visible text, placed amid station-update content
findings.fix: Remove the control if unused, or if intentional, clarify what item it deletes and ensure Enter/Space activation is implemented.
findings.location: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">`
findings.violation: A "Delete item" control is contextually unrelated to anything else on this rider-updates page, and as a custom `role="button"` it has no evident keyboard-activation handling (Enter/Space) in the document.

findings.evidence: three `<div class="step">` entries ("Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", "Confirm your order") with no current-step indicator
findings.fix: Mark up as an ordered list with `aria-current="step"` on the active step, and verify this wizard belongs in this section at all.
findings.violation: The steps use plain `div`s instead of list semantics and have no `aria-current` or similar marker, so screen readers can't convey progress or that these are a sequence; the content (a payment/order wizard) is also unrelated to "Station updates."

findings.evidence: `click here`
findings.fix: Change the link text to something descriptive, e.g. "view the full list of upcoming adjustments".
findings.violation: "click here" is non-descriptive link text; users navigating by a screen reader's links list get no indication of the link's destination or purpose.

findings.evidence: `<form id="s3-form">` (no `action` or `method` attribute)
findings.fix: Add explicit `action` and `method` attributes.
findings.violation: The form has no `action` or `method`, so submitting it has undefined/default behavior (typically a GET to the current URL, discarding intended data).

findings.evidence: options "Northbound"/"Southbound" vs. the table's zones "North"/"South"
findings.fix: Use consistent naming between the table and the form options.
findings.violation: The route selector uses different naming ("Northbound"/"Southbound") than the status table's zones ("North"/"South"), making it unclear whether they refer to the same areas.

findings.evidence: `<select id="topic">`, `<input id="email" ...>`, `<input id="phone" ...>`, `<input id="promo" ...>` - none have a `name` attribute
findings.fix: Add appropriate `name` attributes to each form control.
findings.violation: None of the form controls have a `name` attribute, so on submission their values won't be included in the submitted form data (only `id` is set, which servers don't read).

findings.evidence: label text "(required)" with `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">` having no `required` or `aria-required` attribute
findings.fix: Add `required` (and optionally `aria-required="true"`) to the phone input.
findings.violation: The label visually/textually indicates the field is required, but nothing in the markup enforces or exposes that to assistive technology or form validation.

findings.evidence: `aria-invalid="true"` present on initial page load, before any user interaction
findings.fix: Only set `aria-invalid="true"` dynamically after a failed validation attempt.
findings.violation: Marking the field invalid by default tells screen-reader users there's an error before they've even entered anything, which is confusing and incorrect.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">` followed by `<span class="error-text" aria-live="polite" id="s3-form-promo-error">`
findings.fix: Add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the promo input.
findings.violation: The error message is not programmatically associated with the promo input (no `aria-describedby`), so screen-reader users won't hear it when focusing the field.

findings.evidence: error text states "Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only," but the input has no `maxlength` or `pattern`
findings.fix: Add `maxlength="6"` and a `pattern` (e.g. `pattern="[A-Za-z0-9]{6}"`) matching the stated rule.
findings.violation: The stated validation rule isn't enforced anywhere in the markup, so the field will accept any input regardless of the described format.

findings.evidence: visible text "Submit" vs. `aria-label="Send form now"`
findings.fix: Remove the `aria-label` or change it to include the visible text, e.g. `aria-label="Submit form"`.
findings.location: `<button type="submit" class="btn-primary" id="s3-form-submit" aria-label="Send form now">Submit</button>`
findings.violation: The accessible name ("Send form now") doesn't contain the visible label text ("Submit"), violating WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name and breaking voice-control users who speak the visible label.
